findings.evidence: assert_ CALL SITES ARE UNCHANGED BY THIS COMMIT. Measured at ed9ea91: `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*assert_'` gives 221 on .claude/scripts/tests/workflow-doctor.test.sh and 221 on `git show 32b12b2:.claude/scripts/tests/workflow-doctor.test.sh`. All 58 added spec lines are printf diagnostics. `grep -n 'assert_[a-z_]*' <spec> | grep -i 'measured|binary'` returns NOTHING; positive control on the same input with the same invocation shape, `... | grep -i 'validated set'`, returns lines 1318/1320/1400, so the search works. SILENT-DEGRADATION MEASUREMENT: the shim parse `sed -n 's|^exec \(.*\) "$@"$|\1|p'` is coupled to mk_bd_shim's `printf 'exec %s "$@"\n'` (workflow-doctor.sh:561). Fed a file whose exec line does not match that exact shape, sed prints nothing and exits 0 (measured against `exec /some/bd "$@" # trailing comment` -> empty, rc 0; against a missing file -> empty). `_bd_shim_target` is then empty, the `&&` does not fire, and live_bd_path stays `$WORKDIR/bin/bd` -- an mktemp path deleted when the doctor exits. No error, no marker, no assertion goes red. The repo's six sibling parsers of the same construct (.claude/tests/component/specs/qa-gate.sh:498,805,1125,1228; verify-before-stop.sh:1723; approve-idempotency.sh:443) all use the more tolerant `s/^exec \(.*\) "\$@".*/\1/p` plus `tr -d "\"'"` plus `head -1`, because the component tier's own mk_bd_shim (.claude/tests/component/lib/shim.sh:124) writes `printf 'exec %q "$@"\n'` -- %q, not %s. The new parse is the only one of the seven anchored strictly.
findings.description: The disclosure is CORRECT today -- I verified it end to end on both arms (see the record's notes). The finding is about durability, not correctness: the half that carries the actual answer (`-> /Users/edk0/.local/bin/bd`) is produced by a parse coupled to another function's printf format, with zero assertions pinning either side. A change to mk_bd_shim's format -- including the obvious future hardening of %s to %q, which would fix the pre-existing space-in-path break in that shim -- degrades the disclosure to naming only a temp wrapper, silently and greenly. That is the same 'a check that did not run looks like one that passed' shape the task exists to close, relocated one level down. Does NOT block v5.0.0 under the stated stop rule: it makes no shipped claim false today and breaks no check. v5.0.1 follow-up.

That record justified info on the grounds that 'today's detail is a single ~130-char line so it cannot bite'; the DRIFT detail is now ~380 characters because this commit appended `[measured binary: ...; store: ...]` to it, and the new line's cap is 300 rather than 400, so it bites on the first failing run. findings.evidence: SHIM RESOLUTION IS SINGLE-HOP BY CONSTRUCTION. The `-> target` expansion is guarded by `[ "$live_bd_path" = "$WORKDIR/bin/bd" ]`, so it unwraps the doctor's own wrapper and stops. If the binary behind it is itself a wrapper the chain is not followed. This is reachable in this repo today: .claude/tests/component/lib/shim.sh's mk_bd_shim installs a `bd` wrapper at `<fixture>/bin/bd` and mk_fixture prepends that directory to PATH, so a doctor run inside a component fixture resolves real_bd to that wrapper and would report `<workdir>/bin/bd -> <fixture>/bin/bd`, naming a script rather than the binary that answered. SEPARATELY MEASURED, and the reason this is low rather than info: `command -v` reports the PATH entry, never the symlink target -- with `ln -sf <real>/bd <link>/bd`, `env PATH=<link>:... bash -c 'command -v bd'` printed the <link> path while the file executed was <real>. Homebrew, asdf, mise and the GitHub toolcache all resolve bd through exactly that shape.
findings.description: Every rendering here is TRUE -- the named path is genuinely what resolved -- so this is a precision bound, not an error, and the harness dump already compensates on the failure path by printing `type -a` plus each candidate's own --version. It is recorded because the bound sits directly on the wyt3 question: in a lane where bd reaches PATH through a symlink or a second wrapper, the one new line an operator will read names the link, and closing the gap still needs `ls -l` or `readlink -f`. Does NOT block v5.0.0. v5.0.1 follow-up.

findings.evidence: MEASURED, with a control. The dump runs `"$_bd_cand" --version` unbounded for EVERY bd `type -aP` returns, including rivals the doctor itself never executes. With a second bd on PATH that sleeps 6s before answering, the extracted block took 6s; with the same rival removed from PATH, 0s. Both candidates were still enumerated correctly. The exposure is bounded by run-tests.sh's SPEC_TIMEOUT_S (default 900, and its header states a timeout is 'a FAILURE with a distinct reason -- never a pass'), so a genuinely wedged rival costs one spec's wall clock and fails loudly rather than hanging the tier. The doctor's own `bd --version` at workflow-doctor.sh:1429 is likewise unbounded and pre-existing; what is new is executing binaries the doctor never runs.
findings.description: Recorded for completeness against the brief's hang question, not as a defect. The answer to 'can the harness dump fail or hang the suite' is no: it is failure-path-only, every host-shape I constructed exits 0, and the worst case is a bounded spec timeout that counts as a failure.

Positive control: the same snapshot instrument fired on a deliberate `touch`. The line is present at 32b12b2 (`git show 32b12b2:... | grep -n 'READ-ONLY'` -> line 1415), so it is pre-existing. REAL-WORLD IMPACT IS NIL: `.beads/.gitignore:11` ignores `embeddeddolt/`, and this repo's store already has `.dolt/stats`, which is why a full suite run left `git status --porcelain` empty.
findings.description: Not a finding against this change set -- the diff neither introduces nor relies on the claim, and the new harness dump's own dolt call lands in an mktemp fixture that is cleaned up on exit.
